commit_subject: fix(pdf): a Banner résumé whose band is longer than a page prints its page number on page 1 too (R2-147-pn)
commit_body:
Cause: react-pdf's splitNodes (@react-pdf/layout) has one branch that drops the fixed elements after a node: a page's own child that cannot break and is taller than a page is kept whole on the page, and every later sibling, the fixed page-number footer included, goes to the next page. Every other branch carries the later fixed nodes along. Banner was the only résumé template whose header (the band, wrap={false}) stood straight on the page; every other template nests its unbreakable name row in a breakable View. So a band longer than a page printed no 'Page 1 of N'.

Fix: the Banner's band sits in a plain breakable View, as the other templates' headers do. When the band is longer than a page, react-pdf now splits that View, and the page-level loop goes on to the fixed footer and keeps it on page 1. The footer stays the last child, so it is still each page's last text drawn and text readers still read the name first on page 1. A band that fits a page lays out exactly as before: the View has no style, so it adds no room and moves no break. The note in PdfPage.jsx about this limit now states the rule instead.

Test: 94-page-numbers renders a Banner résumé with a job title many lines long, so its band runs past page 1. It checks that every page prints one 'Page n of N' and that the number is the page's last text drawn. Without the fix, page 1 has no number.
notes: Confirmed at d11d5a0 by reading node_modules/@react-pdf/layout/lib/index.js splitNodes: in the `!fitsInsidePage && !canWrap` branch, currentChildren.push(child) and nextChildren.push(...futureNodes) are followed by a break, with no currentChildren.push(...futureFixedNodes). The other break branches do push them. The root cause is in the library, but patching @react-pdf/layout needs a yarn patch, and its yarn.lock checksum can only be made by running yarn, which the rules forbid here. So the fix makes sure no résumé template puts an unbreakable node straight on the page. Banner's band was the only one: I grepped every wrap={false} under src/templates/pdf/, and each other template's header row, and each section heading and entry, is nested in a breakable View. For a nested unbreakable node, react-pdf splits the parent, and the page-level loop still reaches the fixed footer. The cover letter has one page-level unbreakable node (the closing and signature), but the letter never prints page numbers, so it is out of scope. The 'last text drawn' order is kept: the footer is still the page's last child. Product call: a band longer than a page is still cut off at the paper's edge, as before (the name row never splits). Only the missing number is fixed. I ran no tests (the owner's rules). The test's page-1 footer check relies on pdf.js splitting the 8 pt footer from the overflowing title lines into separate items (a font-size change flushes a text item), as the existing footer tests already assume. docs/knowledge states nothing about this, so no doc change.
